title: Context-aware mini-wizard for cache & batch policy setup
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Ship a compact, context-aware configuration wizard that helps engineers pick safe, cost-effective caching and batching presets when they create or edit inference routes. Scope covers a 3-step UI microflow, inline explainers, recommended presets, and non-blocking guardrail warnings. This ticket captures the final prototype, stakeholder review notes, accessibility checks, acceptance criteria, and rollout guidance.

Design goals:
- Reduce time-to-config for common workloads (conversational chat, single-turn generation, embeddings) to < 90s for first-time users.
- Surface clear trade-offs (latency vs cost vs quality) with microcopy and simple visuals.
- Offer conservative defaults with explicit opt-in for aggressive cost-saving knobs (aggressive batching, KV prefetching).
- Ensure recommendations are explainable and traceable in the console audit trail.

Scope out of this ticket:
- Backend implementation of prefix-KV caching mechanisms (ENG owns).
- Dedicated enterprise-only RBAC gating (handled in PM roadmap).
acceptance_criteria: A compact 3-step wizard prototype exists in Figma with flows for 3 workload personas: chat (low latency), streaming generation (balanced), bulk embeddings (throughput).
Microcopy for each recommended preset explains expected latency and per-token cost direction in plain language (< 2 sentences).
Guardrail modal appears when user selects an aggressive preset, listing potential risks and a quick rollback link.
Prototype includes an accessibility audit note (WCAG AA color contrast checks and keyboard-only flow).
Design handoff includes tokens and component specs and a prioritized QA checklist for console-2026.03 release.
design_notes:
Sketch rationale: prefer a horizontal 3-card stepper (Persona -> Recommendation -> Preview) rather than a long vertical form so users can see trade-offs and preview cost delta at each step. The preview pane shows simulated 1-minute throughput and estimated token cost change. We intentionally clamp recommendations for orgs with Dedicated plans to use stricter defaults.

Microcopy examples included inline in the prototype. We mapped each preset to a runtime-1.18 recommendation profile: 'Conservative (latency-first)', 'Balanced', 'Aggressive (cost-saving, higher latency)'. Each profile maps to kernel selection, batch size targets, and kv-prefetch toggles (implementation references in ENG-2841).
usability_findings: Moderated testing (n=6 engineers) — participants preferred the 3-step card layout; three testers misinterpreted 'prefetch' terminology. Recommended swap to 'KV prefetch (helps for similar conversations)'.
Participants wanted explicit link to 'simulate cost over 1M tokens' from the preview, added as a low-friction CTA.
Keyboard navigation tests revealed focus skip on the guardrail details accordion; added ARIA attributes and focus trapping in prototype.
review_comments: PM (Ravi Kapoor) 2026-03-12: 'Love the conservative defaults. Please add a telemetry flag so we can measure adoption by persona.'
Eng (Lina Gomez) 2026-03-13: 'Design matches planned runtime flags but need to add a 'preview exact kernel/quantization' developer view for Dedicated customers.'
Security (Jamal Brooks) 2026-03-13: 'No sensitive data exposure; please include wording that KV prefetch does not persist customer prompts to third-party services.'
Design (Marco Liu) 2026-03-14: 'Updated microcopy and accessible color tokens; pushing to In Review.'
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Users may over-select aggressive presets to save cost and experience latency spikes. Mitigation: prominent guardrail warnings and opt-in confirmation with consequences.
Risk: Misunderstanding around KV prefetch persistence. Mitigation: explicit footnote and link to privacy docs; add telemetry event to monitor opt-ins.
Risk: Preset mismatch for enterprise Dedicated workloads. Mitigation: surface a 'Developer view' toggle that shows exact runtime knobs and kernel hints for advanced users.
next_steps: Address PM request for telemetry flag (PM-438) — add event names in handoff doc.
Add developer view mockups and link to ENG-2841 for runtime mapping.
Run a 10-user unmoderated study to validate the new wording for 'prefetch'.
Prepare design tokens and export components to the console design system package for QA.
notes_for_engineering: Map presets to runtime profiles documented in ENG-2841; ensure telemetry events are emitted for preset chosen, guardrail dismissed, and simulation CTA clicked.
Provide a lightweight 'developer view' toggle outputting a JSON blob of runtime flags for QA and Dedicated customers.
Guardrail confirmation should be non-blocking but recorded in audit logs with the user's ID and timestamp.
